subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event AI-safety taxonomy, manifest permission field, and host-mediated plugin emission API as permanent public contracts?
rationale: The taxonomy names, plugin SDK surface, manifest policy, trust semantics, and session attribution become durable compatibility and security boundaries; code review cannot choose those contracts without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound API
options.body: Approve the capability in principle, but require the authority, manifest parsing, payload validation, session identity, browser wiring, documentation, and installed-plugin proof to be corrected before merge.

options.title: Narrow to internal diagnostics
options.body: Keep the taxonomy core-internal initially and defer third-party plugin emission until real detector implementations establish the required public contract.

options.title: Reject the series
options.body: Decline the permanent taxonomy and plugin policy surface and close the linked issue and companion PR series with the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound API
recommendation.body: Approve the capability in principle, but require the authority, manifest parsing, payload validation, session identity, browser wiring, documentation, and installed-plugin proof to be corrected before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to plugin API, manifest, service lifecycle, and browser runtime architecture.
